page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside the lines "faba, hordeo", "Carnes pro glandium" and "Monta-". Below the last line: the catchword "locisq;" at the right, and the signature "Gg 5" at the left.

main_text.p: mali terrestri, quo homo vescitur, carnem habent humidiorem, sanguinis à phlegmate viscosi comitem. Differentiam hanc apud Homerum Eumæus Subulcus Vlyssis, quem ex bello Troiano & naufragio sibi tum ignotum, reducem hospitio excepit, obseruat dicens, Ede ô hospes, nam hæc choerea, porcellorum carnes, debentur & supersunt famulis, proci verò Penelopes obesos, & spumantes sues adultos edunt, qui delphaces dicebantur, sicenim nominabant sues corpus robore compactum habentes, & qui adolescant. Ut autem carnes suauitatem adipiscantur & iucunditatem, adq; pinguedinem sues adolescant, glande maximè aluntur, Sagina suum notanda.faba, hordeo, cæterisque frumentis, facilè enim ad quoduis pabulum assuefcunt. Vrbium pisto-res frugum farina & furfuribus saginant ad tantam sæpe pinguitudinem, ut vix loco se mouere queant, & si alio quis transferre velit, plaustro id faciendum esse. Pinguedo & adeps horum, aptissimum aliarum escarum condimentum est. Carnes pro glandium natura variare certum est: fagineam enim su-Suilla caro pro pabuli & glandii ratione variat.em hilarem facere, carnem coctibilem, leue, & stomachoque utilem: ilignam suem nitidam, angustam, ponderosam: quernam diffusam, grauissimam, certi autores tradunt. page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are reconstructed from the scan: "Sagina" and "suum notanda" (beside "faba"), and "Suilla caro pro pabuli & glandii ratione variat." (beside "Carnes pro glandium"). Exact wording of the notes is doubtful at the hyphenated line ends. The signature "Gg 5" is uncertain: the scan shows a long-s-like character, which may be a numeral 5. The word "adolescant" is doubtful at its first occurrence in the line. "Montanorum" is split across lines as "Monta-norum" in print. Several line-end syllables are hard to read at the edges of the scan.
